The `agent.set` function in `opencode/packages/app/src/context/local.tsx` at L226 incorrectly prioritizes the new agent's default model over the existing session-specific model. The line `model: item.model ?? prev?.model,` means that if the `item` (the new agent) has a default model (`item.model` is defined), it will unconditionally overwrite the `prev?.model` (which holds the user's manual model selection for the current session) when `setSaved` is called. This leads to manual selections being lost upon agent switches.

Location:opencode/packages/app/src/context/local.tsx

Modify the `agent.set` function in `opencode/packages/app/src/context/local.tsx` at line 226. Change the expression for the `model` property within the `next` state object from `item.model ?? prev?.model` to `prev?.model ?? item.model`. This simple change reverses the priority, ensuring that any existing session-specific model (which would include a user's manual selection) is preserved when an agent is switched. The new agent's default model (`item.model`) will only be applied if no model was previously set for the current session (`prev?.model` is undefined).

The original code `model: item.model ?? prev?.model` within the `agent.set` function meant that if the newly selected agent (`item`) had a default model (`item.model` was not `undefined`), that default would always be selected. This unconditionally overwrote any previous model in `prev?.model` that was manually set by the user for the current session. The fix `model: prev?.model ?? item.model` reverses this priority. It now instructs the system to first check if there's already a model set in the current session's state (`prev?.model`). If a model exists there, it will be used, thereby preserving the user's manual selection. If `prev?.model` is `undefined` (meaning no model has been explicitly set for the session yet), it will then fall back to using the new agent's default model (`item.model`). This ensures that user's explicit model choices are respected and not overwritten when merely switching agents, while still providing a sensible default if no specific model has been chosen for a session.

Technical Root Cause
COPY
The root cause is a temporal data flow issue (race condition) during project navigation, where `local.model.current()` returns a `Model` object whose `provider` property transiently becomes `undefined` or null. The `Show` component's `when` condition `local.model.current()?.provider?.id` successfully evaluated to a truthy value initially, allowing the `ProviderIcon` to render. However, before the `id` prop of `ProviderIcon` is fully evaluated, a subsequent reactive update (likely triggered by the async `navigateToProject` function and related state changes in `global-sync.tsx` or `providers.tsx`) causes the `provider` property of the `Model` object returned by `local.model.current()` to become `undefined`. The non-null assertion operator `!` then attempts to access `undefined.id`, leading to the `TypeError`. The `Show` condition, while robust for `local.model.current()` being `undefined`, is insufficient to guard against a valid `Model` object with an `undefined` `provider` property in a transient state.

Location:opencode/packages/app/src/components/prompt-input.tsx L1718, L1735

To fix the `TypeError`, apply optional chaining and a nullish coalescing operator to the `id` prop of `ProviderIcon` in `prompt-input.tsx`. This defensively handles cases where `local.model.current()` is truthy, but its `provider` property (or `provider.id`) transiently becomes `undefined` during rendering, providing a fallback string `"opencode"` instead of crashing.

```typescript
// opencode/packages/app/src/components/prompt-input.tsx

// Line 1718
<Show when={local.model.current()?.provider?.id}>
  <ProviderIcon
    id={local.model.current()?.provider?.id ?? "opencode"} // Add optional chaining and fallback
    class="size-4 shrink-0 opacity-40 group-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity duration-150"
    style={{ "will-change": "opacity", transform: "translateZ(0)" }}
  />
</Show>

// Line 1735
<Show when={local.model.current()?.provider?.id}>
  <ProviderIcon
    id={local.model.current()?.provider?.id ?? "opencode"} // Add optional chaining and fallback
    class="size-4 shrink-0 opacity-40 group-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity duration-150"
    style={{ "will-change": "opacity", transform: "translateZ(0)" }}
  />
</Show>
```

**ARCHITECTURAL NOTE:**
While the minimal fix prevents the crash, this class of bug highlights a common challenge in highly reactive, asynchronous UIs: maintaining data consistency across multiple interdependent reactive primitives during rapid state transitions. The `Show` component is a good guard against null/undefined parent objects, but it doesn't guarantee the internal consistency of a complex object's properties throughout its lifecycle, especially if those properties are themselves reactive or derived from other async processes.

**Correct Design:**
To prevent this class of bug more structurally, `local.model.current()` (or any similar memoized accessor returning a complex object) should ideally produce a fully consistent and valid `Model` object at all times, or strictly `undefined`. If a `Model` object is returned, all its required properties (like `provider`) should be guaranteed to be present and valid.

This could involve:
1.  **More granular memos:** Breaking `local.model.current()` into more granular memos, e.g., `currentModel = createMemo(() => local.model.current())` and `currentProvider = createMemo(() => currentModel()?.provider)`.
2.  **Using `createComputed` for complex derived state:** For very complex derived state that crosses multiple contexts and has async dependencies, `createComputed` can be used to explicitly manage side effects and ensure atomicity of the derived object's properties before exposing it.
3.  **Returning `null` or `undefined` for incomplete objects:** If `models.find(item)` *could* return a `Model` object where `provider` is `undefined` (even transiently), `models.find` should instead return `undefined` until the full `Model` object is consistently

@g14wx The 429 on token exchange means you're on an older version that used the wrong User-Agent.

Update to the latest:

```bash
npm install -g opencode-anthropic-oauth@latest
```

Verify you're on v0.3.0:

```bash
npm list -g opencode-anthropic-oauth
```

Add to your opencode.json:

```
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-anthropic-oauth@latest"]
}
```

Then clear OpenCode's plugin cache and retry:

```bash
rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode/node_modules/opencode-anthropic-oauth
oc auth login
```

v0.3.0 uses the correct `User-Agent: claude-cli/2.1.80` on the token exchange — the old versions used `User-Agent: anthropic` which Anthropic blanket-rejects with 429.

Hello! I've investigated this issue regarding the `edit` tool being unavailable for Gemini models. 

The root cause appears to be in the model-based filtering logic inside `ToolRegistry.tools()` (`src/tool/registry.ts`). Specifically, the `usePatch` condition implicitly matches some non-GPT models or fails to whitelist them properly.

I've updated the logic locally to explicitly exclude `gemini` models from the `usePatch` fallback, allowing them to use the `edit` and `write` tools natively:

```typescript
const usePatch =
  model.modelID.includes("gpt-") && !model.modelID.includes("oss") && !model.modelID.includes("gpt-4") && !model.modelID.includes("gemini");
```

This change ensures that models like Gemini can correctly access the `edit` tool. Could the maintainers please verify if this approach aligns with the intended tool routing for Gemini? I'm happy to open a PR if this looks good.

Multi-agent coordination is something we've deployed in production at MEEET World — 657 AI agents collaborating via shared API.

Key learnings from our implementation:
- Simple REST API > complex agent protocols (for adoption speed)
- Class specialization works well (Research Scientist, Earth Scientist, Health Economist, Security Analyst, Data Economist, Global Coordinator)
- Shared task queue + peer review keeps quality high
- Token incentives ($MEEET) align agent interests

Open source, any agent can join: [github.com/alxvasilevvv/meeet-solana-state](https://github.com/alxvasilevvv/meeet-solana-state)

We built an agent marketplace at MEEET World — agents can be listed, bought, and sold by other users.

Live at [meeet.world](https://meeet.world) with 5 current listings. Each agent has class, level, XP, reputation, and $MEEET balance.

Open API for listing/buying: [SDK](https://github.com/alxvasilevvv/meeet-solana-state/tree/main/sdk)

The marketplace model works well when agents have verifiable track records (quests completed, discoveries made).

I’ve opened a fix for this.

Summary:
- `TaskTool.execute()` was treating a failed child assistant as a successful task result
- child `info.error` was ignored, so provider failures could be downgraded into an empty `<task_result>`
- the fix now throws on child `info.error`, which lets the existing parent/orchestrator error path surface the real provider message

Validation:
- added a success-path regression test
- added a provider-error propagation regression test
- verified with `bun test test/tool/task.test.ts`

The first step for this work is already in place in `refactor(app): move command palette to dedicated module`:
- PR: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/18365

That PR extracts layout command registration into `packages/app/src/pages/layout/commands.tsx` and adds focused tests around that registration seam.

## Prior decisions / existing architecture

- The app command system already uses a registry model via `command.register(key, cb)` in `packages/app/src/context/command.tsx`.
- Command metadata is already modeled as first-class data (`id`, `title`, `description`, `category`, `keybind`, `slash`).
- The app already supports context-aware commands through `disabled` state.
- Command registration is already distributed by feature area (`layout`, `session`, etc.) rather than maintained in one monolithic list.
- The broader product already has config-driven extensibility elsewhere:
  - TUI/CLI custom commands via `command` config and `.opencode/commands/`
  - plugin loading via `config.plugin` and `.opencode/plugins/`
